questions.q: What does filtering WHERE is_user_process = 1 accomplish in a query against sys.dm_exec_sessions?
options: It strips out SQL Server's own internal background sessions, leaving only real client connections
It shows only sessions currently blocked by another session
It limits results to sessions with sysadmin permissions
It filters out sessions that are currently running a query
questions.explain: is_user_process = 1 excludes SQL Server's internal system sessions so you see only actual client logins.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between sys.dm_exec_sessions and sys.dm_exec_connections?
options: Sessions represent the logical login context; connections represent the underlying network-level link
Sessions only exist for Windows Authentication logins, connections only for SQL logins
Connections track query text, while sessions track index usage
There is no difference — they return identical columns
questions.explain: sys.dm_exec_sessions is about the logical login session; sys.dm_exec_connections is about the physical network connection it rides on.

questions.q: In the combined sessions/connections/requests query, why use LEFT JOIN to sys.dm_exec_requests rather than an inner JOIN?
options: Because a session with nothing currently executing has no matching row in sys.dm_exec_requests, and LEFT JOIN keeps that session in the results anyway
Because INNER JOIN is not supported against dynamic management views
Because LEFT JOIN runs faster on every SQL Server edition
Because sys.dm_exec_requests requires LEFT JOIN syntax by definition
questions.explain: An idle session has no active request row; an inner join would silently drop it from the results, while LEFT JOIN preserves it with NULLs for the request columns.

questions.q: Which DMV would tell you the client IP address a session connected from?
options: sys.dm_exec_connections
sys.dm_exec_sql_text
sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats
sys.databases
questions.explain: sys.dm_exec_connections includes client_net_address, the network address the connection originated from.

questions.q: What does the status column in sys.dm_exec_sessions tell you?
options: Whether the session is running, sleeping, or dormant — a session can be logged in and idle without executing anything
The exact SQL Server edition installed on the instance
Whether the session's database is online or offline
The recovery model of the database the session is connected to
questions.explain: status distinguishes an actively running session from one that is simply connected and idle (sleeping or dormant).
